travel-mode.heading: Travel Mode.
travel-mode.headingItalic: Full charge for the trip. Back to your cap after.
travel-mode.body: Sensei normally holds your charge at the cap you set (80% suggested) so the battery ages slower. The night before a flight, tap Travel Mode. Sensei lifts the cap, charges to 100%, switches to stricter low-battery warnings (30% / 15% / 5%), and pauses Apple's Optimized Battery Charging. The next morning at 9 AM your normal limit comes back automatically. No reminder to undo it. No battery sitting at 100% for weeks.
travel-mode.mockupCaption: Limit lifted to 100%. Auto-resets tomorrow at 9 AM.
travel-mode.why: Lithium-ion batteries age faster when held at 100%. A typical "top up before a trip and forget" leaves a MacBook at full charge for weeks, measurably aging the cells. The 9 AM auto-reset is the safety net: even if you forget, the cap returns.

custom-thresholds.heading: Custom thresholds.
custom-thresholds.body: The three included presets cover most days, but if you want 22% Warning for 14 s and 6% Alert until acknowledged, you can build exactly that. Sensei lets you set the exact percent for each escalation level and how long each card stays on screen. Per-tier, not one global number.
custom-thresholds.mockupCaption: Info · Warning · Alert. Each with its own percent and dismiss time.
custom-thresholds.why: One global warning threshold can't serve someone on a long-haul flight and someone in back-to-back meetings the same way. Per-tier thresholds let the nudges fit the day.

alert-presets.heading: Alert presets.
alert-presets.headingItalic: Zen Mode. Regular Mode. Teach Me Senpai.
alert-presets.body: Zen Mode whispers at 15% (closes in 5 s) and once more at 5% (10 s), quiet enough to let you finish. Regular Mode adds a red overlay at 5% and a persistent alert at 2%. Teach Me Senpai keeps it simple but stern: a red overlay at 15% and a full-screen alert at 5%, both staying until you dismiss. Pick the mood that fits, or compose your own with Custom thresholds.
alert-presets.mockupCaption: Three preset moods. One tap to switch, any time.
alert-presets.why: macOS gives you exactly one battery notification: at 10%. By then it's often too late for the slide you were about to ship. Three presets let the warning match the stakes.

battery-journal.heading: MacBook battery history.
battery-journal.headingItalic: Cycles, charges, rescues, all in context.
battery-journal.body: Saga is the long view of your battery's life. A charge history chart you can flip between 24 h / 3 d / 7 d, a Battery Health panel (capacity, cycles, temperature, condition), the top power-hungry apps over the last hour / day / week, and Wrapped-style Weekly + Monthly recaps. When you rescue a battery in time (plug in within 30 minutes of a critical warning), Sensei creates a Rescue Receipt: a small, shareable card to mark the save.
battery-journal.mockupCaption: Lifetime stats, charge history, Wrapped recaps. All on the Saga page.
battery-journal.why: Battery numbers without context are just numbers. "92% capacity" tells you nothing. Saga gives the same number a story: what it looked like a week ago, which apps cost it the most, which day you nearly lost it.

meeting-battery-guard.heading: Meeting Battery Guard.
meeting-battery-guard.headingItalic: Know before your battery becomes the problem.
meeting-battery-guard.body: A Premium feature. Included in the free trial, then part of a Lifetime unlock. Opt-in. Sensei reads the next 4 hours of calendar events on-device (EventKit, default lookahead). It scores each meeting against your current battery (Comfortable, Tight, Critical, or Catastrophic) and only nudges when it should. Critical: 30 / 15 / 5 / 1 min before, with the exact minute the laptop would die and the fix ("22 min on the charger and it lasts through the meeting"). Catastrophic: warned immediately. Tight: a single 30-min nudge. Comfortable: silent. Plug in early enough and pending warnings cancel themselves. Titles stay readable in notifications by default; one toggle redacts them.
meeting-battery-guard.mockupCaption: 4-hour lookahead. Only nudges when it should.
meeting-battery-guard.why: A 10% warning mid-meeting is useless: you can't leave to find a charger. Reading your calendar lets Sensei warn you when there's still time to fix it, and stay silent the rest of the time.

energy-usage.heading: Per-app battery drain.
energy-usage.headingItalic: See which apps cost the most.
energy-usage.body: On the Saga page, Sensei ranks the top power users. Flip between the last 1 hour, 24 hours, or 7 days. Each app gets an Activity-Monitor-style energy impact score (CPU time blended with idle wake-ups), an impact label (Low / Moderate / High / Very high), and a search filter so you can find every Chrome helper in the list. Sampled every 5 minutes via per-process resource usage. No system extension, no kernel hooks.
energy-usage.mockupCaption: Top apps · 1h / 24h / 7d · with search filter. Refreshed every 5 min.
energy-usage.why: Battery loss is almost never the battery's fault. It's a hung helper, a sleepless tab, a video call that won't release the GPU. Knowing which app costs you the most is the difference between a 4-hour day and a 7-hour day.

privacy.title: What we collect.
privacy.intro: Battery Sensei is a small, indie macOS app. We collect the minimum needed to run the site, take payments, and notify you about new versions, and we tell you exactly what that means in plain language below.

tldr.heading: The short version

do.1: Run the Mac app entirely on your device. Your battery history and your calendar event titles never leave your Mac.
do.2: Measure website traffic with cookieless, anonymous analytics — aggregate counts only, no tracking cookies.
do.3: Keep only the details you actively hand us: your email if you sign up, your message if you use the contact form, and your purchase (handled by Polar).
do.4: Use a few well-known processors for hosting, payments and email — each one named below with a link to its policy.

dont.1: Sell, rent or share your data with advertisers — ever.
dont.2: Run ad or social-media trackers, embed tracking pixels or sharing widgets, set third-party tracking cookies, or profile you across sites.
dont.3: Build profiles about you or make automated decisions that affect you.
dont.4: Require an account or a login to use the app.

tldr.note: There is no cookie banner because we set no tracking cookies. Downloads and in-app updates are served from GitHub, which sees your IP address like any web server. The full detail is below.

controller.heading: Who's responsible for your data
controller.p1: Battery Sensei is operated by <0>Sandro Thabiso Schaier</0>, self-employed individual (živnostník), with business seat at Korunní 2569/108, 101 00 Prague 10, Czech Republic. References to "we" / "us" on this page mean that operator.
controller.p2: Contact for any privacy-related question, request, or complaint: <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We try to reply within a working day.

app.heading: What the macOS app does on your Mac
app.p1: Battery Sensei is a native macOS app that runs entirely on your Mac. Reading your battery, your charging, and the next few hours of your calendar all happens on-device — none of it passes through a server we operate.
app.p2: The app contains no telemetry, no analytics SDK, no crash reporter and no cloud account. Your battery history is stored only on your Mac. Calendar event titles are read locally to time your meeting alerts and never leave your device.
app.p3: The only network connection the app makes on its own is an update check: it periodically fetches an update feed (an "appcast") from battery-sensei.app to see whether a newer version exists. That request reaches our host the same way any web request does, appears only in short-lived server logs, and carries no account or device identifier. If an update is available, the new version is downloaded from GitHub — see the next section.

github.heading: Downloading the app and its updates
github.p1: We host the app's installer and its release notes in a public GitHub repository (<0>github.com/schaier-io/battery-sensei-releases</0>). When you click "Download for Mac", or when the in-app updater installs a new version, your device connects directly to GitHub to fetch the file. No GitHub account is required.
github.p2: Like any web server, GitHub receives your IP address, the file you requested and your browser's user-agent in order to serve the download, and may log that data and set its own cookies if you browse the repository in a browser. For this connection <0>GitHub, Inc.</0> (a Microsoft company) acts as an independent controller under its own privacy statement. We never receive a list of who downloaded the app.
github.p3: GitHub's handling of these requests is governed by the <0>GitHub Privacy Statement</0>. If you open an issue or comment on the repository, whatever you write — and your GitHub username — is shared with GitHub and is publicly visible.

what.heading: The full list, by surface
what.intro: This section is about the marketing website at battery-sensei.app and the order flow on it — the app itself is covered above and collects nothing. On the website we keep data to a minimum:

items.localeBody: a first-party cookie called <0>bs_locale</0>, written only after you change language via the site switcher. Stores your two-letter locale (e.g. <0>de</0>), expires after one year, never shared.
items.purchaseBody: a session-scope sessionStorage entry called <0>bs_purchase_tracked</0> that prevents duplicate conversion events when you refresh the thank-you page. Cleared the moment you close the tab.
items.analyticsBody: anonymized pageview counters and Core Web Vitals via Vercel Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights, plus a single anonymous "purchase complete" event on the thank-you page (which plan you bought, and the Polar order reference) so we can count completed checkouts. No cookies, no cross-site identifiers; visitor IP addresses are hashed once at the edge before any storage.
items.signupBody: only if you submit the "get the download" form: the email address you typed, the locale of the page, your IP and user-agent (for abuse triage), plus a timestamp.
items.contactBody: only if you write to us via the contact form: name, email, message subject and body, plus IP / user-agent / referring origin for spam protection.
items.checkoutBody: only if you click Buy: the Polar checkout iframe collects your billing details directly. We never touch the card number; we only see what Polar reports back to us (email used, country, receipt id, fulfillment status).
items.logsBody: short-lived request logs at Vercel containing path, status, user-agent and a truncated IP. Used for debugging and abuse triage. Vercel rotates these on a rolling 30-day window.

why.heading: Purpose and legal basis

items.functionalBody: language cookie, purchase-confirmation flag. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) and Recital 30 of the ePrivacy Directive (strictly functional storage).
items.orderBody: checkout data, license key delivery, refund handling. Legal basis: <0>performance of contract</0> (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
items.newsletterBody: only the email addresses you explicitly submit through the signup form, confirmed by double opt-in (we email you a link and add you only once you click it). Legal basis: <0>consent</0> (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), withdrawable at any time via the unsubscribe link in every email, or by writing to <1>info@battery-sensei.app</1>.
items.analyticsBody: a minimum signal of "the site is up and people are reading it". Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in operating and improving the service. No profiling, no advertising re-targeting.
items.abuseBody: IP and user-agent on the contact and signup forms. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in protecting the service from spam, scraping and fraudulent purchase attempts.

why.noAutomated: We do not engage in any automated decision-making or profiling with legal or similarly significant effects on you (Art. 22 GDPR).

processors.heading: Who stores your data
processors.intro: We use a small set of processors. Each has its own privacy policy, linked below. No data we hold is sold or shared with advertising networks.

items.vercelBody: US-based hosting provider, serves the site, runs the server functions, hashes IPs at the edge. Vercel is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Policy: <0>vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.polarBody: merchant of record for all purchases. Handles payment processing, VAT, refunds, license issuance. Card data is collected directly by Polar; we never see it. Transfers to Polar (US) rely on Standard Contractual Clauses. Policy: <0>polar.sh/legal/privacy</0>.
items.resendBody: sends release-alert and transactional emails (purchase receipt, key resend, contact-form confirmation). Email addresses you submit through our forms are mirrored to Resend audiences. Transfers to Resend (US) rely on Standard Contractual Clauses; Resend is also self-certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Policy: <0>resend.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.postgresBody: serverless PostgreSQL host (Neon, LLC), provisioned through the Vercel Marketplace. Holds the newsletter-signup table and the contact-form table; the database lives in the EU (AWS, Frankfurt / eu-central-1). Your purchase and license records are not stored here — those are held by Polar. Neon, LLC is covered by Databricks' EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification, and any transfers also rely on Standard Contractual Clauses. Policy: <0>databricks.com/legal/privacynotice</0>.

items.signupBody: kept while you stay subscribed. If you unsubscribe, we keep your address on a short suppression record so we honour your opt-out and don't silently re-add you if the form is submitted again; you can ask us to erase it entirely at any time.
items.contactBody: kept up to 24 months from the last reply on the thread, then purged.
items.purchaseBody: Polar, as merchant of record, retains the underlying tax invoice and license record for the legally required period (typically 10 years under Czech Act No. 563/1991 Coll.). We do not keep a copy of your purchase or license in our own database; when you need support we look it up in Polar by order id.
items.logsBody: rotated by Vercel within 30 days of the request.

rights.heading: What you can ask us to do
rights.intro: Under the GDPR (and the Czech Act No. 110/2019 Coll.) you have the right to:

items.access: Request <0>access</0> to the personal data we hold about you (Art. 15 GDPR).
items.correct: Ask us to <0>correct</0> data that is inaccurate or incomplete (Art. 16).
items.delete: Ask us to <0>delete</0> your data when it's no longer needed (Art. 17). For purchase data we have to retain accounting records under Czech tax law.
items.restrict: Ask us to <0>restrict</0> processing while a correction is being assessed (Art. 18).
items.portable: Receive a <0>portable copy</0> of your data in a machine-readable format (Art. 20).
items.object: <0>Object</0> to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21).
items.withdraw: <0>Withdraw consent</0> at any time. The unsubscribe link is at the bottom of every newsletter email.

rights.closing: To exercise any of these rights, email <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We will reply within one month of receipt and may extend this by up to two further months for complex requests, in which case we will notify you within the first month and explain why. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů, <1>uoou.gov.cz</1>) or with the data protection authority in your country of residence.

changes.heading: When this page is updated
changes.p1: When we change a material practice (a new processor, a different retention window, a new type of data collected), we update the "last updated" date at the top of this page. If a change affects your consent (for example, a new newsletter type), we will email you separately and ask before opting you in.
